Let
\[
\Delta=a^2d^2-6abcd+4ac^3+4b^3d-3b^2c^2.
\]
I claim
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[\Delta].}
\]

Set
\[
E=\frac{X+Y}{2},\qquad F=\frac{X-Y}{2},\qquad H=Z.
\]
Then
\[
[H,E]=2E,\qquad [H,F]=-2F,\qquad [E,F]=H,
\]
so \(E,F,H\) form an \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-triple. Their action on \(A=k[a,b,c,d]\) is
\[
E(a)=0,\ E(b)=a,\ E(c)=2b,\ E(d)=3c,
\]
\[
F(a)=3b,\ F(b)=2c,\ F(c)=d,\ F(d)=0,
\]
\[
H(a)=3a,\ H(b)=b,\ H(c)=-c,\ H(d)=-3d.
\]

A direct calculation gives
\[
E(\Delta)=F(\Delta)=H(\Delta)=0.
\]
Since \(a,b,c,d\) commute pairwise, this means \(\Delta\) commutes with \(a,b,c,d,E,F,H\), hence with \(a,b,c,d,X,Y,Z\). Therefore
\[
k[\Delta]\subseteq Z(R).
\]

It remains to show there are no other central elements. Give \(R\) its PBW filtration. Then
\[
\operatorname{gr}R\simeq S(\mathfrak{sl}_2\ltimes V),
\]
where \(V=\langle a,b,c,d\rangle\) is abelian. If \(u\in Z(R)\), then its top symbol \(\sigma(u)\) lies in the Poisson center of \(S(\mathfrak{sl}_2\ltimes V)\).

Let \(P\) be Poisson central. From \(\{a,P\}=\{b,P\}=\{c,P\}=0\), the partial derivatives of \(P\) with respect to \(X,Y,Z\) vanish, because the relevant coefficient matrix has nonzero determinant
\[
-6(a^2d-3abc+2b^3).
\]
Thus \(P\in k[a,b,c,d]\). So the Poisson center is just the ring of \(\mathfrak{sl}_2\)-invariants in \(k[a,b,c,d]\).

Now compute those invariants. Localize at \(a\), and set
\[
p=c-\frac{b^2}{a},\qquad
q=d-\frac{3bc}{a}+\frac{2b^3}{a^2}.
\]
Then \(E(p)=E(q)=0\), so any invariant lies in \(k[a,a^{-1},p,q]\). The remaining \(F\)- and \(H\)-conditions reduce to
\[
q\frac{\partial P}{\partial p}-\frac{6p^2}{a}\frac{\partial P}{\partial q}=0,
\qquad
3a\frac{\partial P}{\partial a}-p\frac{\partial P}{\partial p}-3q\frac{\partial P}{\partial q}=0.
\]
The first equation has polynomial solutions generated by
\[
a^2q^2+4ap^3.
\]
But
\[
a^2q^2+4ap^3=\Delta.
\]
The \(H\)-condition then forces the coefficients to be constants, hence
\[
k[a,b,c,d]^{\mathfrak{sl}_2}=k[\Delta].
\]

Therefore the Poisson center of \(\operatorname{gr}R\) is \(k[\Delta]\). By induction on the PBW degree, subtracting the matching polynomial in \(\Delta\) from any central element lowers its degree, so every central element of \(R\) lies in \(k[\Delta]\).

Hence
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k\!\left[a^2d^2-6abcd+4ac^3+4b^3d-3b^2c^2\right].}
\]
